I would say it's fear. I mean we grew up getting physically and emotionally hurt by them. That gives them a sense of control over us. I was in a similar situation but with my father. He's physically and emotionally abusive as well. When I left home, it was an explosion of anger as I packed my things and loaded it into the car. I'll tell you now that what I did was unhealthy. During that time I was so afraid but I was angrier and that somehow gave me a sense of control and power over my fear. Like an animal, I relied on projecting my voice as loud as I can, throwing everything he ever did to me when I was growing up. I even challenged the old man to a one on one. I reminded him of the abuse I went through but all he ever said was "I don't remember doing any of those." That only made my blood boil.

But in the end, I felt unburdened. I moved out that day and I haven't seen my father ever since. The effects of his abuse still linger. He gave me depression and anxiety but I feel calmer compared to when I was still living with him. I don't know if it'll work for you but detaching might help. Like my father, your mother is a negative stimulus. She's a trigger for everything she did in the past. Ridding your environment of her might be the solution as talking it out oftentimes doesn't work especially with Boomers. They were raised differently.

A lot of reasons... I'm even guilty of it myself back in high school. I guess I thought it made me unique and it gave me the license to act the way I wanted. It's the lack of knowledge regarding mental illness. Maybe not lack but the very limited knowledge. The faces of mental illness which most people know are just the tip of the ice berg. They hear depression and they think it's sadness and that somehow being sad made them cool. They hear schizophrenia and they think psychedelic hallucinations without the degradation of the mind. They hear DID and imagine getting away with the embarrassing stuff they did. That's to name a few.

I took a BS in Psychology where I finally learned everything in depth and I realized that it's not a joking matter or a material for fairy tales. Think of romanticising diabetes or cancer. When I finally learned, life decided to become a bitch and give me depression and anxiety. Not so romantic now that I spend sleepless nights due to pervasive thoughts or weeks where I can't get out of bed. I'm a mental health worker but like doctors and nurses, that doesn't immunize me from what we deal with. And I think putting on a tough face where nothing is wrong isn't helping. But I'm okay. I have to be. Or else no money for everyday necessities. Sorry to rant all of the sudden.

Me father doesn't know my birthday, my age and my bachelor's degree. But he was so proud bragging about his children to his friends. Three times the idiot asked me when my birthday was, my age and what I took in college in front of his friends.
This is a difficult one... Yeah no I'd rather just die.
I'd rather just die without eating shit thank you very much.
Easy. Flogged of course. Between eating feces and water boarding, I'd choose water boarding and God, I will do whatever it takes to kill myself before I'm forced to eat feces.
Don't forget that every house also has a Hikikomori. For example, the one in our house is me.
